newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Amnesty urges Manila to scrap death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty urges Manila to scrap death penalty.

text.p: Amnesty International urged the Philippines on Friday not to execute a man convicted of raping his daughter, warning it "could unleash a flood" of other executions in the country.

Prison officials said they expected to finish construction next month of an execution chamber. About 300 people have been sentenced to death by local courts for crimes ranging from rape and kidnapping to murder and drug trafficking since the death penalty was restored in 1994 .

The Supreme Court, which must confirm all the death sentences before they are carried out, has so far confirmed only that imposed by a judge in 1994 on house painter Leo Echegaray for raping his 10-year-old daughter.

"We fear the first execution could unleash a flood. An average of 12 people are being sentenced to death each month in the Philippines - one of the highest rates in the world," the Asia section of the London-based group said in a statement.

Amnesty released at a news conference its report published last month pointing to the region of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) as an exception to what it said was a worldwide trend towards abolition of the death penalty.
The report said concern about the death penalty in the region was partly due to the failure of ASEAN governments to release information about executions.
"In several of the countries executions have been carried out in secret. The lack of official statistics means that the true number of executions remains unknown," the report said.
"Amnesty International urges the ASEAN countries to call a halt to any further executions and to work towards abolition of the death penalty," the report said.

The Philippines abolished the capital punishment in 1987 but restored it in 1994. There has been no execution in the country for the past two decades and Echegaray, 38, could be the first to be executed under the new law unless he is a granted presidential clemency.
